newsitem.title: FRANCE: French premier vows to fight left and extreme right.
newsitem.headline: French premier vows to fight left and extreme right.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said his centre-right coalition would fight both the left and the extreme right when it faces them in general elections scheduled in a year's time.

"Let's not make a mistake about who are our adversaries. In (March) 1998, we shall have to simultaneously fight against the rightist extremism of some and the (leftist) irresponsibility of others," he told a congress of locally-elected officials on Saturday.

Unveiling what appeared to be his campaign tactics for the general election, Juppe said: "Between the speech of hate of some and the demagogy of others, we are the only ones who can incarnate a true policy of healthy, balanced and humanistic change."

Juppe's Rally for the Republic (RPR) Gaullists and their junior partners of the centre-right Union for French Democracy (UDF) will face Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right National Front and a Socialist-led opposition at the polls.
Le Pen wants millions of immigrants expelled while some left-wingers want France opened to unfettered immigration. Juppe's government wants to block any new mass immigration.
